paragraphs: Unless the context otherwise indicates, references to "we," "us," "our" and "the Company" refer to Barnes & Noble Education, Inc. or "BNED", a Delaware corporation. References to "Barnes & Noble College" or "BNC" refer to our subsidiary Barnes & Noble College Booksellers, LLC. References to "MBS" refer to our subsidiary MBS Textbook Exchange, LLC.

Our fiscal year is comprised of 52 or 53 weeks, ending on the Saturday closest to the last day of April. "Fiscal 2026" means the 52 weeks ended May 2, 2026, and "Fiscal 2025" means the 53 weeks ended May 3, 2025. "Fiscal 2027" means the 52 weeks ended May 1, 2027.

Barnes & Noble Education, Inc. ("BNED") is one of the largest contract operators of physical and virtual bookstores for college and university campuses and K-12 institutions across the United States. We are also one of the largest textbook wholesalers and inventory management hardware and software providers. As of May 2, 2026, we operated 1,116 physical and virtual bookstores, delivering essential educational content and general merchandise within a dynamic omnichannel retail environment.

The strengths of our business include our ability to compete by developing new products and solutions to meet market needs, our large operating footprint with direct access to students and faculty, our well-established, deep relationships with academic partners and stable, long-term contracts and our well-recognized brands. We provide product and service offerings designed to address the most pressing issues in higher education, including enhanced convenience and improved affordability through innovative course material delivery models designed to drive improved student experiences and outcomes. We offer our BNC First Day® affordable access course material programs, consisting of First Day Complete and First Day, which provide faculty required course materials on or before the first day of class at below market rates, as compared to the total retail price for the same course materials if purchased separately (a la carte), and students are billed the below market rate directly by the institution as a course charge or included in tuition. These programs have allowed us to reverse historical long-term trends in course materials revenue declines, which has been observed at those schools where such programs have been adopted, and improve predictability of our future results. Many institutions adopted First Day Complete in Fiscal 2026, and we plan to continue to scale the number of schools adopting First Day Complete in Fiscal 2027 and beyond.

We expect to continue to introduce scalable and advanced solutions focused largely on the student and customer experience, expand our e-commerce capabilities and accelerate such capabilities through our service providers, Fanatics Retail Group Fulfillment, LLC ("Fanatics") and Fanatics Lids College, Inc. D/B/A "Lids" ("Lids", and together with Fanatics, referred to herein as the "F/L Relationship"), win new accounts, and expand our revenue opportunities through strategic relationships. We expect gross comparable store general merchandise sales to increase over the long term, as our product assortments continue to emphasize and reflect changing consumer trends, and we evolve our presentation concepts and merchandising of products in stores and online, which we expect to be further enhanced and accelerated through the F/L Relationship. Fanatics and Lids, acting on our behalf as our service providers, provide unparalleled product assortment, e-commerce capabilities and powerful digital marketing tools to drive increased value for customers and accelerate growth of our logo general merchandise business.

The Barnes & Noble brand (licensed from our former parent) along with our subsidiary brands, BNC and MBS, are synonymous with innovation in bookselling and campus retailing, and are widely recognized and respected brands in the United States. Our large college footprint, reputation, and credibility in the marketplace not only support our marketing efforts to universities, students, and faculty, but are also important to our relationship with leading publishers who rely on us as one of their primary distribution channels.

We provide product and service offerings designed to address the most pressing issues in higher education, including enhanced convenience and improved affordability through innovative course material delivery models designed to drive improved student experiences and outcomes. We offer our BNC First Day® affordable access course material programs, consisting of First Day Complete and First Day, which provide faculty-required course materials to students on or before the first day of class at below market rates, as compared to the total retail price for the same course materials if purchased separately (a la carte), and students are billed the below market rate directly by the institution as a course charge or included in tuition.

•First Day Complete is adopted by an institution and includes all or the majority of undergraduate classes (and on occasion graduate classes), providing students both physical and digital materials. The First Day Complete model drives
substantially greater unit sales and sell-through for the bookstore.
•First Day is adopted by a faculty member for a single course, and students receive primarily digital course materials through their school's learning management system ("LMS").

Offering course materials through our BNC First Day® affordable access course material programs, First Day Complete and First Day, is an important strategic initiative of ours to meet the market demands of reduced pricing for students, as well as the opportunity to improve student outcomes, while, at the same time, increasing our market share, revenue and relative gross profits of course material sales given the higher volumes of units sold in such models as compared to historical sales models that rely on individual student marketing and sales. These affordable access course material programs have allowed us to reverse historical long-term trends in course materials revenue declines, which has been observed at those schools where such programs have been adopted. We continue to move quickly to accelerate our First Day Complete strategy. Many institutions adopted First Day Complete in Fiscal 2026, and we plan to continue to scale the number of schools adopting First Day Complete.
During the 52 weeks ended May 2, 2026, BNC First Day® total revenue increased by $166.3 million, or 28.0%, to $760.1 million compared to $593.8 million during the prior year period.

headings: Risks Relating to our Business and Industry
We are dependent upon access to the capital markets, bank credit facilities, and short-term vendor financing for liquidity needs.
We face significant competition for our products and services, and we expect such competition to increase.
Our business depends on our ability to attract and retain talented employees, including senior management.
We may not be able to enter into new managed bookstore contracts or successfully retain or renew our managed bookstore contracts on profitable terms.
We face the risk of disruption of supplier relationships.
We face the risk of fluctuating inventory supplies as a consequence of changes in the way publishers distribute course materials.
Our wholesale business may not be able to manage its inventory levels effectively, which may lead to excess inventory or inventory obsolescence.
Our business is dependent on the overall economic environment, college enrollment and consumer spending patterns.
Tariffs or other restrictions placed on imports, and any ensuing trade wars may have a material adverse impact on our financial condition and results of operations.
Our business is seasonal.
Our international operations could result in additional risks.
Risks Relating to our Strategic Plan
We intend to offer new products and solutions to students to grow our business. If our efforts are not successful, our business and financial results would be adversely affected.
Risks Relating to Data Privacy, Information Technology and Cybersecurity
We face potential data privacy and information security risks with respect to unencrypted, non-deidentified personal information.
Computer malware, viruses, hacking and phishing attacks could harm our business and results of operations.

Defects, errors, installation difficulties or performance issues with our point-of-sales and other systems could expose us to potential liability, harm our reputation and negatively impact our business.
Risks Relating to Applicable Laws and Regulations
Laws and regulations have been and may be enacted in the future that restrict or prohibit the use of emails or similar marketing activities that we currently rely on.
Our business could be impacted by changes in federal, state, local or international laws, rules or regulations.
Recent actual and proposed federal policy changes and enforcement practices could negatively impact college students, and our client educational institutions.
Changes in tax laws and regulations might adversely impact our businesses or financial performance.
Expectations regarding environmental, social, and governance matters may affect our business.
Risks Relating to Intellectual Property
We rely on third-party digital content and applications, which may not be available to us on commercially reasonable terms or at all.
We may not be able to adequately protect our intellectual property rights or may be accused of infringing upon intellectual property rights of third parties.
paragraphs: The risks and uncertainties set forth below, as well as other risks and uncertainties described elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K (this "Form 10-K") including in our consolidated financial statements and related notes and "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" or in other filings by BNED with the SEC, could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and the trading price of our common stock. Additional risks and uncertainties that are not currently known to us or that are not currently believed by us to be material may also harm our business operations and financial results. Because of the following risks and uncertainties, as well as other factors affecting our financial condition and operating results, past financial performance should not be considered to be a reliable indicator of future performance, and investors should not use historical trends to anticipate results or trends in future periods.

We must have sufficient sources of liquidity to fund working capital requirements. The combination of cash-on-hand, cash flow received from operations, funds available under our credit agreements and short-term vendor financing must be sufficient to meet our normal working capital and debt service requirements. In addition, we may require additional capital in the future to sustain or grow our business, including implementation of our strategic initiatives. The future availability of financing will depend on a variety of factors, such as economic and market conditions, and the availability of credit. Additional financing may not be available to us on favorable terms when required or at all. Failure to secure adequate financing when required could lead to going concern issues, the consequences of which would have a severe negative impact upon our business. These factors could also materially adversely affect our costs of borrowing, and our financial position and results of operations would be adversely impacted. Volatility in global financial markets may also limit our ability to access the capital markets at a time when we would like, or need, to raise capital, which could have an impact on our ability to react to changing economic and business conditions. Accordingly, if the economy worsens, our business, results of operations and financial condition could be materially and adversely affected. If we raise additional funds through the issuance of equity, equity-linked, or debt securities, those securities may have rights, preferences or privileges senior to the rights of our common stock, and our stockholders may experience substantial dilution. There can be no assurances that such financing can or will be obtained at any time in the future if needed.

In addition, as noted above, our liquidity is dependent in part on the availability of funds under our credit agreements. If we are not able to comply with the covenants under our credit agreements, we may need to seek consents, waivers and/or amendments to our credit agreements from our lenders to avoid an event of default thereunder. Although we have been successful in negotiating consents, waivers and/or amendments to our credit agreements, we may be unsuccessful in negotiating any further consents, waivers and/or amendments to any such agreements as we may deem necessary. Further, the terms of any such consents, waivers and/or amendments may be less favorable than the current terms of our credit agreements or may impose additional restrictions on the operations of our business. Under such circumstances, our business and liquidity could be materially and adversely affected. See Part II - Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data - Note 2. Basis of Presentation and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies.

We operate within a competitive and rapidly changing business environment, in general, and each of our lines of business faces competition for the products and services they offer. We face competition from other college bookstore operators and educational content providers, including Follett Corporation, eCampus, University Gear Shop, Valore Campus, Textbook Brokers, Slingshot, and BibliU. Our online/virtual course material store operations also face competition from providers including eCampus, Akademos, and Ambassador Educational Solutions. We also face competition from other third-party sellers and local bookstores, as well as direct-to-student platforms including, Amazon, bn.com, the e-commerce platform of Barnes & Noble, Inc.; Chegg.com, an online textbook rental company; and publishers, including Cengage Learning, Pearson Education and McGraw-Hill Education, which bypass the traditional retail distribution channel by selling directly to students and institutions. We face competition from e-Textbook/digital content providers, VitalSource Technologies, Inc., and Red-Shelf. Our wholesale business competes with Amazon, GoTextbooks, and Texas Book Company. Competitors that compete with our general merchandise offerings include Amazon, Sodexo and Aramark, online retailers, physical and online office supply stores and local and national retailers that offer college-themed and other general merchandise. Students often purchase from multiple textbook providers, are highly price sensitive, and can easily shift spending from one provider or format to another. As a consequence, in addition to being competitive in the services we provide to our customers, our textbook business faces significant price competition. Some of our competitors have adopted, and may continue to adopt, aggressive pricing policies and devote substantial resources to marketing, website and systems development. In addition, a variety of business models are being pursued for the provision of print and digital textbooks, some of which may be more profitable or successful than our

business model, including our BNC First Day® affordable access course material models. Furthermore, the market for course materials is diluted from counterfeiting and piracy of digital and print copies or illegal copies of selected chapters made by students or others; user-generated and faculty-created content; and sharing or non-purchase of required course materials by students.

We have encountered and will continue to encounter these risks and, if we do not manage them successfully, our business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects may be materially and adversely affected.

paragraphs: 除非文意另有所指，文中所稱「我們」、「我們」、「我們」及「本公司」均指 Barnes & Noble Education, Inc. 或「BNED」，為一間設立於特拉華州的公司。文中所稱「Barnes & Noble College」或「BNC」均指我們的子公司 Barnes & Noble College Booksellers, LLC。文中所稱「MBS」均指我們的子公司 MBS Textbook Exchange, LLC。
我們的會計年度包含 52 或 53 週，於每年四月最後一天最近的星期六結束。『財務 2026』指 2026 年 5 月 2 日結束的 52 週，『財務 2025』指 2025 年 5 月 3 日結束的 53 週。『財務 2027』指 2027 年 5 月 1 日結束的 52 週。
Barnes & Noble Education, Inc.（「BNED」）是美國各大專院校與大學校園及 K-12 教育機構中，規模最大的實體與虛擬書店經營商之一。我們同時也是規模最大的教科書經銷商與存貨管理硬體與軟體供應商。截至 2026 年 5 月 2 日，我們經營 1,116 家實體與虛擬書店，於動態的全通路零售環境中，提供學生與教職員工必要的教育內容與一般商品。

我們業務的優勢包括我們能透過開發新產品與解決方案來競爭以符合市場需求、我們擁有廣大的營運據點並可直接接觸學生與教師、我們與學術機構有著長期且穩固的關係與穩定的長期契約，以及我們備受認可的品牌。我們提供的產品與服務方案旨在解決高等教育中最重要的問題，包括透過創新課程材料交付模式來提升便利性與降低成本，以改善學生的學習體驗與成果。我們提供 BNC First Day® 這項可負擔的課程材料方案，包含 First Day Complete 與 First Day，這些方案讓教師所需的課程材料能在開學前或開學第一天前以低於市場價格提供給學生，與若學生單獨購買（a la carte）相同課程材料的總零售價格相比，學生會由學校直接以低於市場價格的費用計入課程費用或包含在學費中。這些方案已使我們逆轉過去課程材料收入下降的長期趨勢，這在採用這些方案的學校中已觀察到，並提升我們未來結果的可預測性。許多機構在財務 2026 年採用了 First Day Complete，我們預計在財務 2027 年及以後會持續擴大採用 First Day Complete 的學校數量。

我們預期會持續推出可擴展且先進的解決方案，主要聚焦於學生與客戶的體驗，擴展我們的電商能力，並透過我們的服務供應商 Fanatics Retail Group Fulfillment, LLC（「Fanatics」）與 Fanatics Lids College, Inc. D/B/A 「Lids」（「Lids」，與 Fanatics 合稱為「F/L Relationship」）來加速這些能力的發展，爭取新的客戶，並透過戰略合作關係擴大我們的收入機會。我們預期在長遠的未來，我們的可比店家一般商品銷售額會增加，因為我們的產品組合持續強調並反映消費者趨勢的變化，我們也會持續改進商店與線上的產品展示概念與商品陳列，而我們預期這些改進會透過 F/L Relationship 進一步強化與加速。Fanatics 與 Lids 作為我們的服務供應商，代表我們提供無與倫比的產品組合、電商能力與強大的數位行銷工具，以提升客戶價值並加速我們的標誌一般商品業務成長。
Barnes & Noble 品牌（由我們的前母公司授權）與我們的子公司品牌 BNC 與 MBS，均與書店與校園零售的創新密切相關，並在美國廣為認可與尊重的品牌。我們在各大專院校的廣大營運據點、市場聲譽與可信度，不僅支持我們對大學、學生與教師的行銷努力，同時也對我們與領導出版社的關係至關重要，因為這些出版社依賴我們作為他們主要的分銷通路之一。

我們提供的產品與服務方案旨在解決高等教育中最重要的問題，包括透過創新課程材料交付模式來提升便利性與降低成本，以改善學生的學習體驗與成果。我們提供 BNC First Day® 這項可負擔的課程材料方案，包含 First Day Complete 與 First Day，這些方案讓教師所需的課程材料能在開學前或開學第一天前以低於市場價格提供給學生，與若學生單獨購買（a la carte）相同課程材料的總零售價格相比，學生會由學校直接以低於市場價格的費用計入課程費用或包含在學費中。
•First Day Complete 由機構採用，並包含所有或大多數的本科課程（有時也包含研究生課程），為學生提供實體與數位材料。First Day Complete 模式驅動
書店的單元銷售量與銷售通路大幅增加。
•First Day 由一名教師用於單一課程，學生主要透過學校的學習管理系統（"LMS"）取得數位課程資料。

透過我們的 BNC First Day® 可負擔性課程資料方案，包括 First Day Complete 和 First Day，是我們重要的戰略計畫，以回應學生降低價格的市場需求，同時也有機會提升學生學習成果，同時增加我們的市場佔有率、營業收入及課程資料銷售的毛利率，因為這些模式的銷售單元數量較以往依賴個別學生行銷與銷售的模式更高。這些可負擔性課程資料方案已使我們逆轉過去在課程資料收入方面的長期下降趨勢，這種趨勢在採用這些方案的學校中已經觀察到。我們持續加速推進 First Day Complete 策略。許多機構在會計年度 2026 中採用了 First Day Complete，我們計畫持續擴大採用 First Day Complete 的學校數量。
於 2026 年 5 月 2 日結訖之 52 週期間，本公司 BNC First Day® 營業收入較前一會計期間之 593.8 百萬美元增加 166.3 百萬美元，成長 28.0%，達 760.1 百萬美元。

paragraphs: 除非文意另有所指，否則文中所稱「我們」、「我們」、「我們」及「本公司」均指 Barnes & Noble Education, Inc. 或「BNED」，為一 Delaware 公司。文中所稱「Barnes & Noble College」或「BNC」均指我們的子公司 Barnes & Noble College Booksellers, LLC。文中所稱「MBS」均指我們的子公司 MBS Textbook Exchange, LLC。
我們的會計年度包含 52 或 53 週，於每年四月最後一天最近的星期六結束。『財務 2026』指 2026 年 5 月 2 日結束的 52 週，『財務 2025』指 2025 年 5 月 3 日結束的 53 週。
請配合閱讀『關於未來展望陳述的揭露』，以及我們合併財務報表及其附註，內容包含於本年度報告表 10-K（此『表 10-K』）第 15 項項目中。

Barnes & Noble Education, Inc.（「BNED」）為美國各大學校及 K-12 教育機構中，規模最大的實體與虛擬書店合約經營商之一。我們同時也是規模最大的教科書經銷商與存貨管理硬體與軟體供應商。我們經營 1,116 家實體與虛擬書店，於動態的全通路零售環境中，提供必要的教育內容與一般商品。Barnes & Noble 品牌（由我們前母公司授權）與我們的子公司品牌 BNC 與 MBS，對我們與領導出版社的關係至關重要，這些出版社依賴我們作為其主要分銷通路之一。如需詳細說明我們的業務、產品與服務、戰略計畫、關鍵關係與競爭地位，請參閱本表 10-K 第一部分第 1 項「業務」。

本公司業務的優勢包括我們透過開發新產品與解決方案以應對市場需求的競爭能力、我們擁有廣大的營運據點並可直接接觸學生與教師、我們與學術夥伴建立的穩固且深入的關係以及穩定的長期契約，以及我們廣為認知的品牌。我們提供設計用以解決高等教育中最迫切問題的產品與服務方案，包括透過創新課程材料交付模式來實現可負擔的接取、提升便利性與改善可負擔性，以提升學生的學習體驗與成果。我們提供 BNC First Day® 可負擔接取課程材料方案，包括 First Day Complete 與 First Day，這些方案可讓教師在開課前或開課當日即取得所需課程材料，價格低於市場價格，相較於若單獨購買相同課程材料（a la carte）的總零售價格，學生則由學校直接按低於市場價格的費用計入課程費用或包含在學費中。在截至 2026 年 5 月 2 日的 52 週期間，BNC First Day® 總營業收入增加 166.3 百萬美元，或 28.0%，達 760.1 百萬美元，較前一年同期的 593.8 百萬美元成長。這些方案已使我們逆轉過去課程材料收入下降的長期趨勢，此現象在採用這些方案的學校中已觀察到，並提升我們未來結果的可預測性。在 2026 年會計年度，我們 BNC First Day® 方案的成長抵銷了 a la carte 課程軟體銷售與實體店面銷售的下降。我們持續觀察到機構對 First Day Complete 與 First Day 方案的強烈興趣，反映大學與學院持續朝向可負擔接取課程材料模式轉變，以提高學生參與度並改善取得所需課程材料的可近性。

本公司與 Fanatics Retail Group Fulfillment, LLC ("Fanatics") 以及 Fanatics Lids College, Inc. D/B/A "Lids" (合稱 "F/L 關係") 有戰略服務供應商關係，這些關係提供電子商務能力、產品組合專業知識以及數位行銷工具，以加速本公司標誌性一般商品業務的成長。由於標誌及象徵性一般商品銷售由 Lids 和 Fanatics 處理，本公司在合併財務報表中以淨額方式確認這些銷售所產生的佣金收入。有關 F/L 關係的完整說明，請參閱第一部分，第 1 項，業務中的 "與 Fanatics 和 Lids 之關係"。
2024 年 6 月 10 日，本公司完成多項交易 ("交易")，包括一股權權益發行、私人股權投資、定期貸款債務轉換以及信貸融資重組，以大幅降低本公司合併資產負債表的負債。有關這些交易的詳細說明，請參閱第一部分，第 1 項，業務中的 "融資安排" 以及合併財務報表附註中的第 10 項，債務。
本公司根據業務管理方式來辨識應報告分部。目前的董事長 (目前的首席運營決策者 ("CODM")) 會評估表現並分配資源。本公司目前以單一運營及應報告分部運作。

headings: 與我們業務及產業相關之風險
我們依賴取得資本市場、銀行信貸融資及短期供應商融資以應付流動性需求。
我們面臨對我們產品及服務的重大競爭，且我們預期此種競爭將持續增加。
我們的業務取決於我們吸引並留住優秀人才的能力，包括高階管理層。
我們可能無法與電信業者簽訂新的管理書店合約，或成功維持或續約我們的管理書店合約於有利可圖之條件。
我們面臨供應商關係中斷之風險。
我們面臨因出版商分發課程材料方式改變而導致存貨供應波動之風險。
我們的批發業務可能無法有效管理其存貨水準，這可能會導致存貨過多或存貨陳舊。
本公司營運依賴總體經濟環境、大學入學人數及消費者支出模式。
進口所課徵的關稅或其他限制措施，以及由此引發的貿易戰，可能對本公司財務狀況及營運結果造成重大不利影響。
本公司營運具有季節性。
本公司國際業務可能導致額外風險。
與本公司戰略計畫相關的風險
本公司有意提供新產品與解決方案給學生以拓展業務。若本公司努力未獲成功，將對本公司營運及財務結果造成不利影響。
與資料隱私、資訊科技及網路安全相關的風險
本公司面臨與未加密且未去識別化之個人資料相關的資料隱私及資訊安全風險。
電腦惡意軟體、病毒、駭客攻擊及網路釣魚行為可能影響本公司業務及營業成果。
本公司點數銷售系統及其他系統若存在瑕疵、錯誤、安裝困難或效能問題，可能使本公司面臨潛在責任，損害本公司聲譽，並對本公司業務產生負面影響。
與適用法律及法規相關的風險
現行法律及法規已或可能於未來頒佈，限制或禁止本公司目前所依賴的電子郵件或其他行銷活動。
本公司業務可能受聯邦、州、地方或國際法律、規則或法規變動的影響。
近期實際及提案中的聯邦政策變動及執法做法，可能對大專學生及本公司客戶教育機構產生負面影響。
稅法及法規的變動可能對本公司業務或財務表現產生不利影響。
關於環境、社會及治理議題的預期可能影響本公司業務。
智慧財產權相關風險
我們依賴第三方數位內容及應用程式，這些內容及應用程式可能無法以商業上合理的條件或完全無法取得。
我們可能無法充分保護我們的智慧財產權，或可能被指控侵權第三方的智慧財產權
paragraphs: 本文件中所列之風險與不確定性，以及於本年度報告表10-K（本「表10-K」）其他處所描述之其他風險與不確定性，包括於我們合併財務報表及相關附註、『管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析』，或BNED向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）所提交之其他申報文件中所述者，可能會對我們之業務、財務狀況、營運成果及普通股之交易價格產生不利影響。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前尚未為我們所知，或目前未被我們認為具有重大性，也可能對我們之業務營運與財務結果造成損害。由於上述風險與不確定性，以及影響我們財務狀況與營運成果之其他因素，過去之財務表現不應視為未來表現之可靠指標，投資人亦不應以歷史趨勢預測未來期間之結果或趨勢。

我們必須擁有足夠之流動性來支應營運資金需求。現金結餘、營運活動所產生之現金流、信用協議下可取得之資金以及短期供應商融資之組合，必須足夠以支應我們之正常營運資金與債務償還需求。此外，我們未來可能需要額外資金以維持或擴張業務，包括執行我們之戰略計畫。未來取得融資之可能性將取決於多種因素，例如經濟與市場條件，以及信貸之可取得性。我們可能無法在需要時以有利條件取得額外融資，甚至可能無法取得。若無法在需要時取得足夠融資，可能會導致持續營運問題，其後果將對我們之業務產生嚴重負面影響。這些因素也可能對我們之借款成本造成重大不利影響，並對我們之財務狀況與營運成果產生不利影響。全球金融市場之波動也可能限制我們在需要時取得資本市場之能力，這可能會影響我們應對經濟與業務條件變動之能力。因此，若經濟惡化，我們之業務、營運成果與財務狀況可能受到重大且不利之影響。若我們透過發行普通股、普通股連結證券或債務證券來取得額外資金，這些證券可能擁有優先權、偏好權或特權，高於我們普通股之權利，股東可能面臨重大稀釋。

此外，如上所述，我們之流動性部分取決於信用協議下資金之可取得性。若我們無法遵守信用協議下之契約條件，我們可能需要向貸款人尋求同意、豁免或協議變更，以避免觸發違約事件。雖然我們已成功與貸款人協商取得同意、豁免或協議變更，但我們可能無法成功協商任何進一步之同意、豁免或協議變更，以取得我們認為必要之協議。此外，任何進一步之同意、豁免或協議變更之條款，可能不如現有信用協議之條款有利，或可能對我們業務之營運施加額外限制。在這種情況下，我們之業務與流動性可能受到重大且不利之影響。請參閱第二部分 - 第八項 財務報表與補充資料 - 第二節 財務報表之編製基礎與重要會計政策摘要。

我們在一個競爭激烈且快速變動之商業環境中運作，總體而言，我們各業務線均面臨其所提供產品與服務之競爭。我們面臨來自其他大學書店經營者與教育內容供應商之競爭，包括Follett Corporation、eCampus、University Gear Shop、Valore Campus、Textbook Brokers、Slingshot 和 BibliU。我們之線上/虛擬課程材料商店業務亦面臨來自 eCampus、Akademos 和 Ambassador Educational Solutions 之競爭。我們亦面臨來自其他第三方販售者與當地書店，以及直接對學生提供服務之平台，包括 Amazon、bn.com、Barnes & Noble, Inc. 之電子商務平台；Chegg.com，一家線上教科書租賃公司；以及出版商，包括 Cengage Learning、Pearson Education 和 McGraw-Hill Education，這些公司透過直接對學生與機構銷售，跳過傳統零售分銷渠道。我們亦面臨來自 e-Textbook/數位內容供應商，VitalSource Technologies, Inc. 和 Red-Shelf 之競爭。我們之批發業務與 Amazon、GoTextbooks 和 Texas Book Company 競爭。與我們一般商品業務競爭之公司包括 Amazon、Sodexo 和 Aramark、線上零售商、實體與線上辦公用品商店，以及提供大學主題及其他一般商品之本地與全國零售商。學生經常從多個教科書供應商處購買新書，對價格極為敏感，且可輕易地將支出從一個供應商或格式轉移到另一個。因此，除了在為客戶提供服務方面具有競爭力外，我們之教科書業務亦面臨重大價格競爭。我們部分競爭對手已採用，且可能繼續採用，激進的價格政策，並投入大量資源於行銷、網站與系統開發。此外，正進行多種商業模式以提供印刷與數位教科書，其中一些模式可能比我們之商業模式更具利潤或成功。
課程材料市場因學生或他人製作之數位與印刷複製品或非法複製之選定章節、用戶生成內容與教師創作內容，以及學生分享或未購買所需課程材料而被稀釋。
我們已遭遇並將繼續遭遇這些風險，若我們未能成功管理這些風險，我們之業務、財務狀況、營運成果與前景可能受到重大且不利之影響。
